questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I've always been interested in Japan and Japanese culture, and the FrontierLab program at Osaka University allows you to use your ECTS on a scientific project in one of the university's laboratories, which I was very excited about.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The dormitory and university staff provide guidance with all the stuff you need to take care of upon arrival, so even though everything was a bit overwhelming at first (as would be expected in a completely foreing country) it was not difficult to get the necessary things done.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: See previous answer.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: You can apply for the Global Village Tsukumodai university dormitory when you make your exchange application, so it's very easy. If you want to live in a single room rather than a shared unit you can also apply for it separately by following the process shown on the dormitory website (if and when single rooms become available to students), but you have to notify the management that you have made two separate applications.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: For me it was pretty easy to get to campus as I was at Suita campus which is one train stop and a 15 minute walk away from Global Village. Toyonaka campus is a bit farther but still easy to get to by train, just a bit expensive.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Since I was a FrontierLab student, my supervisor took care of the registration process, so communicate with your supervisor. If you are not FrontierLab I'm sure the staff at the Center for International Education and Exchange (CIEE) are happy to help.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: See previous answer.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Successful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: See previous answer.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I only took an elective Japanese language course apart from the laboratory project, so I can't comment on the level of courses related to my field of study.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: In my case the lab supervision was pretty similar to what I have previously experienced in Denmark, apart from some cultural differences. I've heard from other students that this and the workload varies among laboratories though.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: FrontierLab D (30 ECTS), Elective Japanese Language Course (0 ECTS)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I definitely recommend FrontierLab and if you want to also learn some Japanese I suggest to take the creditless elective course so you don't have to worry about passing it.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None that I can think of.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Fruit and vegetables are quite expensive. Eating out can be quite a bit cheaper than cooking your own food (depending on where you go).

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There's a lot of clubs for many different activities at Toyonaka campus, and some student associations organize social gatherings at least once a month. Also Global Village will occasionally organize social events.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Definitely attend dormitory and university welcome parties to get to know people.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: There's so much to see in Japan, even just around the Kansai area. You can easily get to Kyoto, Kobe, and Nara from Osaka.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I would say you get used to it pretty fast, even though in the beginning the manners can seem a bit weird.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Sometimes it can be difficult to get a direct answer from Japanese people, for the sake of politeness.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The orderliness and organization.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. It would help to learn as much Japanese as possible before your exchange (I didn't learn much)
2. Do the FrontierLab program if you're in science, and contact a potential supervisor in advance
3. Use your free time to see as much of Japan as possible, it's a really beautiful country

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Can't think of anything else.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people I met, both Japanese and international students.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The language barrier with the locals.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
